title: The Life of Jesus
description: Thirty days walking through the Gospel of Mark, the shortest and fastest of the four accounts, plus a few scenes the family should not miss. Read it together and watch what Jesus does before you decide what to think of him.

days.prompt: John comes out of the desert and a voice tears open the sky. Ask everyone what they think it would feel like to hear a Father say out loud that he is pleased with you.
Four fishermen drop their nets and follow a stranger. Ask what they had to leave behind, and whether anyone at the table has ever left something good for something better.
Jesus teaches and the room can tell he means it. Ask what is different about a person who speaks like they actually believe what they are saying.
Jesus touches a man no one else would touch. Ask who at school or in the neighborhood gets left out, and what it would look like to go near them.
Friends dig through a roof to get one man to Jesus. Ask each person to name a friend they would carry, and one who has carried them.
Jesus eats dinner with the wrong crowd and the religious people are scandalized. Ask why a doctor spends his time with sick people instead of healthy ones.
The same seed lands on four kinds of ground. Ask honestly which kind of soil each of you feels like this week, and why.
Jesus sleeps through a storm that terrifies grown men. Ask what storm is scaring your family right now, and what it means that he can stand up and tell it to stop.
A man living among the tombs is given his mind and his life back. Ask what the man wanted to do next, and what Jesus told him to do instead.
A sick woman and a dying girl on the same afternoon. Ask why Jesus stopped for one person in the crowd when an important man was waiting.
Five loaves, two fish, and thousands of hungry people. Ask what small thing your family has that God could use if you handed it over.
Jesus walks across the water in the middle of the night. Ask what it tells us that he came to his friends in the part of the night they were most afraid.
A foreign mother will not stop asking, and Jesus heals her daughter. Ask what it looks like to keep praying when the answer feels slow.
A blind man is healed in two stages, seeing partly before he sees clearly. Ask if there is something about God your family is only beginning to understand.
Jesus asks the question the whole book is built around, who do you say that I am. Let each person answer it out loud, even the youngest.
Jesus shines like the sun on a mountain and the Father speaks again. Ask why Peter wanted to stay up there and build something.
A desperate father says I believe, help my unbelief. Ask whether faith and doubt can live in the same heart at the same time.
The disciples argue about who is greatest and Jesus sets a child in front of them. Ask what it means that the kingdom belongs to the small and the overlooked.
Grownups try to keep the children away and Jesus is angry about it. Ask the kids how it feels to know Jesus wanted them close enough to hold.
A rich young man walks away sad because he loves his money more. Ask what your family would have the hardest time giving up if Jesus asked.
Jesus says he came to serve, not to be served. Ask each person to name one quiet way they could serve someone in the house this week.
Blind Bartimaeus shouts until Jesus hears him. Ask why Jesus asked a blind man what he wanted when the answer seemed obvious.
Jesus rides into the city on a borrowed donkey and the crowd goes wild. Ask what kind of king arrives on a donkey instead of a war horse.
Love God with everything and love your neighbor as yourself. Ask which of those two is harder for each person right now.
A poor widow gives two small coins and Jesus says she gave the most. Ask what God measures when he looks at what we give.
Jesus prays in the garden, sweating and afraid, and still says not my will but yours. Ask what it costs to obey when you are scared.
Jesus is arrested and Peter denies he ever knew him. Ask if anyone has ever stayed quiet about something they believed because they were afraid of what people would think.
Jesus dies and a Roman soldier is the one who says this really was the Son of God. Ask why the cross convinced the least likely person in the crowd.
Women come to the tomb with spices and find it empty. Ask what would change about everything if this part is actually true.
Jesus gives Peter, who failed him, the job of feeding his sheep. Ask what it means that Jesus trusts the people who let him down with the work that matters most.

title: Heroes and Promises
description: Thirty days through the big story of the Old Testament, from the first morning of the world to the prophets who pointed ahead to Jesus. Built for kids, with prompts a parent can read straight off the page.

days.prompt: God speaks and a world appears, full of light and water and animals. Ask each child to name their favorite thing God made and why they think he made it.
God makes people in his own image and then rests. Ask what it means that you look a little like the God who made the stars.
The first people listen to a lie and hide from God. Ask what we do when we have done something wrong, and whether hiding ever actually helps.
Even as he sends them out, God makes a promise that someone will one day crush the snake. Ask why God did not give up on people who had just disobeyed him.
Noah builds a huge boat because God told him to, while everyone laughs. Ask what it feels like to obey God when no one else understands.
The water goes down and Noah steps out onto a fresh new world. Ask the kids what they would have said to God if they were the first ones off the boat.
God hangs a rainbow in the sky as a promise. Ask what your family can remember the next time you see one.
God tells Abraham to leave home for a place he has never seen. Ask if anyone has ever had to trust God about something they could not yet see.
God points Abraham to the stars and promises a family too big to count. Ask why Abraham believed God even though he was old and had no children yet.
Abraham trusts God even when the test is terrifying, and God provides a ram. Ask what it means that God gives us what we cannot give ourselves.
Joseph has big dreams and his brothers cannot stand him. Ask what happens in a family when one person feels jealous of another.
Joseph is sold by his own brothers. Ask the kids how Joseph must have felt, and whether God had left him alone in that pit.
Years later Joseph forgives the brothers who hurt him. Ask why Joseph said that what they meant for evil, God meant for good.
God speaks from a bush that burns but does not burn up, and calls Moses by name. Ask what Moses was afraid of, and what God said back to him.
On the night of the Passover, a lamb dies so the people can go free. Ask what this story makes you think of later, when Jesus becomes the Lamb.
The sea opens and the people walk through on dry ground. Ask what your family does when there seems to be no way forward.
God gives ten rules to a people he just rescued. Ask why God gives rules to the children he loves, the way parents do.
God tells Joshua to be strong and brave because he will never be alone. Ask what makes each person brave when they are scared.
The walls of Jericho fall after the people march and trust. Ask what it means to obey God even when the plan sounds strange.
Ruth refuses to leave Naomi and chooses her God as her own. Ask what it means to stay loyal to someone when leaving would be easier.
Ruth, a foreigner, becomes the great grandmother of King David. Ask the kids how God brings outsiders right into the middle of his story.
God picks the youngest, smallest brother to be king. Ask what God looks at when he chooses people, and what people usually look at instead.
David faces a giant with a sling and a steady trust in God. Ask what giant feels too big for your family, and who really won that fight.
The shepherd boy who became king writes about God as his own shepherd. Ask what a good shepherd does for the sheep, and how that feels.
Three friends walk into a furnace and a fourth figure walks with them. Ask who that fourth person might be, and what it means that they were not alone in the fire.
Daniel keeps praying even when it is against the law, and God shuts the lions mouths. Ask what your family would keep doing even if it got hard.
Hundreds of years early, a prophet describes a child who will be called Mighty God and Prince of Peace. Ask who you think he was talking about.
Isaiah describes someone who would be wounded for our wrongs. Ask the kids who carries our mistakes so we do not have to.
A tiny town called Bethlehem is promised a ruler. Ask why God so often starts the biggest things in the smallest places.
The Old Testament ends with a promise that a messenger is coming. Ask what it feels like to wait a long time for something good God has promised.

title: Psalms for the Family
description: Thirty days in the prayer book of the Bible, where people sing, cry, trust, and give thanks out loud. A plan for learning to say true things to God in every kind of weather.

days.prompt: Two ways to live, like a tree by water or like chaff the wind blows away. Ask what keeps a tree standing in a storm, and what your family is planted near.
The same God who set the stars in place still thinks about people like us. Ask why it is good news that someone so big bothers with someone so small.
The sky tells about God without saying a word. Ask each person what the world around them seems to be saying about the one who made it.
The Lord is my shepherd and I have everything I need. Ask what the shepherd does in this psalm, and which line your family needs most today.
Whom shall I fear, asks David, when the Lord is my light. Ask what makes us afraid, and what it would change to remember who is with us.
Taste and see that the Lord is good. Ask everyone to name one good thing from this week that came from God.
The writer is sad and talks to his own soul, asking why it is downcast. Ask if it is alright to be honest with God when we feel low.
God is our refuge even when the mountains fall into the sea. Ask what it means to be still and know that he is God when everything feels shaky.
David has sinned badly and asks God to make him clean again. Ask what we do with the wrong we have done, and where this psalm says to take it.
My soul finds rest in God alone. Ask where each person looks for rest when they are worn out, and where this psalm points instead.
David is in a dry desert and still says God is better than life. Ask what your family is thirsty for, and whether God can satisfy a thirst that water cannot.
The writer almost gives up because bad people seem to win, until he walks into God's presence. Ask what changes when we look at the whole story instead of just today.
Better is one day in God's house than a thousand anywhere else. Ask what place makes your family feel most at home with God.
Moses prays about how short life is and asks God to teach us to count our days. Ask what your family would do differently if we remembered our days are a gift.
The one who lives close to God is kept under his wings. Ask what a baby bird feels under its mother's wing, and what that says about staying near God.
A short, loud song of thanks. Read it twice, then have each person shout out one thing they are thankful for.
God forgives, heals, and removes our sins as far as the east is from the west. Ask how far that is, and what it means that he does not hold our wrongs over us.
A young person asks how to stay clean, and the answer is God's word hidden in the heart. Ask why it helps to memorize what God says.
I lift my eyes to the hills, where does my help come from. Ask who watches over your family while you sleep and never once closes his eyes.
Those who plant in tears will gather in with songs of joy. Ask if anyone has ever cried over something that later turned to joy.
Out of the depths I cry to you, Lord. Ask what it means to call to God from the lowest place, and that he hears us there.
The writer calms his soul like a small child resting on its mother. Ask how a tired child rests, and what it would look like to rest like that with God.
How good it is when a family lives together in unity. Ask what makes a home feel peaceful, and one thing each person could do to add to it.
Every line ends with his love endures forever. Read it as a back and forth, with one person reading and everyone answering that line.
God knows you completely and there is nowhere you can go to leave him. Ask whether being fully known by God feels scary or safe, and why.
God made you carefully and knew you before you were born. Ask each child what it means that they were wanted and planned, not an accident.
A song about how good and kind God is to everyone. Ask everyone to finish the sentence, God is good because.
Do not trust in powerful people, trust in the God who lifts the fallen. Ask who this psalm says God pays special attention to.
The Psalms end with every instrument and every breath praising God. Ask the kids how they would praise God if they could use any sound in the world.
Sing to the Lord a new song. Ask your family to make up one short line of praise of your own and say it together before you finish.

title: Foundations
description: A twenty one day starter plan for a family new to faith or coming back to it. Plain, gentle, and ordered, walking through who God is, who we are, what Jesus did, and how a person follows him.

days.prompt: Before anything else, there was God, and then there was light. Ask what it means to start the whole story with someone who was already there.
The sky points to a maker even to people who have never read a Bible. Ask what your family notices in nature that feels like more than an accident.
People are made in God's image and called very good. Ask what it changes about how we treat each other if every person carries his image.
You were made on purpose and known before your first breath. Ask each person how it feels to be wanted rather than random.
The first people choose their own way over God's, and something breaks. Ask what goes wrong when we decide we know better than the one who made us.
Everyone falls short, and that includes all of us at this table. Ask why it is actually a relief to admit none of us has it all together.
Our wrongs put a distance between us and God. Ask what it feels like to be far from someone you love, and whether God wants it to stay that way.
God did not stay far off, he came and lived among us as a person. Ask what it means that the God of the universe had a face and a name.
The king of everything is born in a barn to a young couple far from home. Ask why God chose to arrive so small and so poor.
Jesus starts his work by saying the kingdom of God is near. Ask what good news your family most needs to hear right now.
A son runs away, wastes everything, and his father runs to meet him anyway. Ask who in this story is most like God, and how the father responds to a child who left.
God loved the world so much he gave his own Son. Ask what is the most you have ever given for someone, and what it means that God gave the most.
On his last night Jesus shares a meal and explains that his body and blood are given for us. Ask why he wanted his friends to remember him with a meal.
Jesus is crucified and forgives the people doing it. Ask what kind of love stays loving even while it is being hurt.
The tomb is empty and death did not get the last word. Ask what would change for your family if this is really true.
Thomas doubts until he sees Jesus for himself. Ask whether it is alright to have questions, and what Jesus does with an honest doubter.
People hear the good news and ask what they should do, and the answer is turn and be baptized. Ask what it would look like to turn toward God this week.
Believing in your heart and saying it with your mouth, anyone who calls on God is welcomed. Ask if there is anything stopping each person from calling on him.
Jesus says stay connected to him like a branch to a vine. Ask what happens to a branch cut off from the plant, and how we stay attached to Jesus.
Jesus teaches his friends a simple prayer. Pray it together slowly, one line at a time, and ask which line means the most to each person.
The first believers learn together, eat together, and share their lives. Ask what step your family could take to be part of a church that lives like this.
